title: Outdoor Recreation Jobs and Economic Impact Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on November 14, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Outdoor Recreation Jobs and Economic Impact Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Commerce to enter into a joint memorandum with the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior to conduct, acting through the Bureau of Economic Analysis, an assessment and analysis of the outdoor recreation economy of the United States and the effects attributable to it on the overall U.S. economy.

In conducting the assessment, Commerce: (1) may consider employment, sales, contributions to travel and tourism, and other appropriate contributing components of the outdoor recreation economy; and (2) must consult with specified federal agency heads and representatives of businesses, including small business concerns, that engage in commerce in the outdoor recreation economy.

No additional funds are authorized to carry out the requirements of this bill. Such requirements shall be carried out using amounts otherwise authorized.

summary.headline: This law directs the Commerce Department to study how much outdoor recreation contributes to the U.S. economy, using existing funds.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Commerce to work with the Departments of Agriculture and the Interior to assess the outdoor recreation economy. The Bureau of Economic Analysis will lead the work and may look at jobs, sales, and travel and tourism spending tied to outdoor activities. Commerce must consult federal agency heads and businesses, including small businesses, in the outdoor recreation field. No new money is provided, so the work must be paid for from funds already authorized.

who_it_affects.group: Outdoor recreation businesses, including small businesses
who_it_affects.how: They must be consulted during the study and may have input into how the economic picture is measured.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies in Commerce, Agriculture, and the Interior
who_it_affects.how: They must coordinate on the joint memorandum and carry out the assessment using existing budgets.

who_it_affects.group: Workers and visitors in outdoor recreation industries
who_it_affects.how: The study may produce data on jobs and spending in this sector, but the law itself does not change their pay, rights, or services.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on December 8, 2016, and the summary does not give a specific deadline for the assessment.
